meta.census_parts: brain/reader, gobbler/reader-ext, demiurge/reader-ext-dm, dynasty/reader-ext-dl, manifold/manifold-reader-ext, drift/drift-ext

Analyser.note: the data outputs are filled once per frame while the node is active (the test rig draws about 3 frames per second in our reader); the window is the last fftSize samples at that moment, so single samples are not compared between the engines, only rms, frequency and the peak bin; smoothingTimeConstant is read back from the audio node, not measured as a time response; the noise floor of the spectrum (bins away from the peak) is not compared
Analyser.prev_note: the data outputs are only fed while the node is active and a Web Audio context exists; nothing is wired into the analyser yet (the Sound children of this node come with the rest of the Sound group); minDecibels, maxDecibels and smoothingTimeConstant go to the audio node when it is made; changing them while it runs is not applied until the next start

Anchor.note: only a #Viewpoint url is followed in the test; any other url goes to body.opts.onAnchor, a page without a handler gets a note and stays where it is (X_ITE 16.6.0 loads the url itself: the bridge never loads a world, that is the host's job); javascript: urls are refused on purpose; target= in parameter is passed to onAnchor, not acted on; autoRefresh and autoRefreshTimeLimit are held, since the bridge loads nothing there is nothing to refresh; the stock body does not report isBound for the first Viewpoint at load (X_ITE does), so the test binds V1 first
Anchor.prev_note: only #Viewpoint urls are followed in the test; other urls go to body.opts.onAnchor, a page without one gets a note and stays; javascript: urls are refused on purpose; addChildren and removeChildren are accepted and not acted on; autoRefresh is not implemented; target= in parameter is passed to onAnchor, not acted on; the stock body does not report isBound for the first Viewpoint at load (X_ITE does), so the test binds V1 first

Arc2D.note: lines are not pickable, so the check is the picture (silhouette overlap and the mean colour of the drawn pixels, SwiftShader CPU raster) plus the segment count between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs through its internal getVertices, a private API) and one line mesh in our body; line width is one pixel in both, ours is an anti-aliased ribbon
Arc2D.prev_note: lines are not pickable, so there is no hit probe: the segment count is compared between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs via its internal getVertices, which is a private API), and our body is checked to have built one line mesh; colour and line width are not compared

ArcClose2D.note: compared by pointer-over probes, the triangle count and the picture; texture mapping and lighting of ArcClose2D are not compared with X_ITE
ArcClose2D.prev_note: compared by pointer-over probes in both engines and the triangle count; texture mapping and lighting are not compared

AudioDestination.note: the audio only plays once the page's audio context is allowed to run (a click or key on the page, or the browser's autoplay flag in the test); this is the browser's rule, not the bridge's; the signal is compared at the node's output stage, not at the loudspeaker (the test browser has no output device), so which physical device a real id reaches is not compared, only that the id is accepted or refused and the signal is unchanged
AudioDestination.prev_note: mediaDeviceID would pick the output device with setSinkId; the bridge's graph ends at the page's default output with no Audio element, so it is held but not applied; the audio only plays once the page's audio context is allowed to run (a click or key on the page); this is the browser's rule, not the bridge's

BallJoint.note: the bridge solves joints as velocity rows with a 0.2 per step error correction; a long chain of joints needs more iterations; anchor outputs are local to each body, as in X_ITE; changing anchorPoint after load does not move the joint (it is fixed from the initial poses); forceOutput ALL raises every output of the node

BiquadFilter.note: the field gain is the input stage (as in X_ITE); the biquad's own gain (what makes PEAKING and the shelves boost or cut) is never set in either engine, so those three types are flat; a time dependent node here only keeps the clock (isActive, isPaused, elapsedTime); the signal passes whether or not it is active, as in X_ITE; the phase response is not compared, only the magnitude
BiquadFilter.prev_note: the filter response is Web Audio's, the same engine under both; only the settings are compared; a time dependent node here only keeps the clock (isActive, isPaused, elapsedTime); the signal passes whether or not it is active, as in X_ITE

BlendedVolumeStyle.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 names the weight functions ALPHA0 / ALPHA1 (first and second volume) while the schema says ALPHA1 / ALPHA2: its ALPHA1 and ONE_MINUS_ALPHA1 write a stray space into the shader (blendColor_ 12 .a) so the whole volume vanishes, and ALPHA2 / ONE_MINUS_ALPHA2 fall back to CONSTANT; the bridge reads the schema names and keeps ALPHA0 as an alias of ALPHA1; two BlendedVolumeStyle nodes in one X_ITE volume (two in a Composed, one inside another) are a GLSL redefinition and draw nothing; the bridge draws any number; the second volume is read through the default ramp (red channel only) as in X_ITE, so its green, blue and alpha never matter; a nested style reads the second volume (its gradient and its alpha), X_ITE rewrite of x3d_Texture3D[0]; only an OpacityMapVolumeStyle is tested nested here; the weight transfer function is read from a PixelTexture only (nearest below 16 texels, first channel)

BoundaryEnhancementVolumeStyle.note: the numbers depend on the 400 slice count and the 8 bit blend of X_ITE for faint samples; the bridge adds up the same alpha in float, the tolerance is 10 levels; pow(0, 0) is hardware defined and is not tested; the surfaceNormals field does not exist on this node

BoundedPhysicsModel.note: colour is compared: a quad particle is lit like a surface (emissive + diffuse x headlight, white for this Material); ours is 255 white, X_ITE 16.6.0's mean over its drawn pixels is about 200 (its edges are blended), fg tolerance 70; no fade at the end of life without a colorRamp (as X_ITE); the bounds are tested in ours from the particle list (a box of 3 x 2 x 2 holds every particle, which reflect at the faces); X_ITE's particle positions are not read, its picture is compared by extent
BoundedPhysicsModel.prev_note: X_ITE 16.6.0 draws the particles white on this raster, ours uses the Material emissive colour (colour is not compared); the bounds are tested in ours from the particle list (a box of 3 x 2 x 2 holds every particle, which reflect at the faces); X_ITE's particle positions are not read, its picture is compared by extent

BufferAudioSource.note: a sound loaded from url is decoded by the browser at the audio context's own rate (44100 Hz in the test rig), so sampleRate and bufferLength read back the resampled values (a 1600 sample 8 kHz file reads 44100 and 8820), identical in both engines; the file formats and the network loading of other schemes than data: are not compared; the field is bufferLength in X_ITE 16.6.0 and bufferlength (lowercase l, output only) in the X3D 4.0 XSD and UOM; both names exist here and the test uses the X_ITE one at run time, because the XSD one cannot be written; a pause stops the source and resume starts it again at the paused position, since a Web Audio buffer source cannot pause; autoRefresh and autoRefreshTimeLimit are held, not acted on; loopStart and loopEnd are set on the source but the looped part is not measured; a url that is not a data: or same-origin file is not fetched in the test; X_ITE 16.6.0 reports bufferDuration -1 (not the UOM's 0) from the start while load is TRUE and nothing has loaded; the bridge does the same
BufferAudioSource.prev_note: the field is bufferLength in X_ITE 16.6.0 and bufferlength (lowercase l, output only) in the X3D 4.0 XSD and UOM; both names exist here and the test uses the X_ITE one at run time, because the XSD one cannot be written; loading from url is written (fetch and decodeAudioData, then numberOfChannels, sampleRate, bufferLength, buffer and bufferDuration are filled in) but not tested here: it needs a sound file; a pause stops the source and resume starts it again at the paused position, since a Web Audio buffer source cannot pause; autoRefresh and autoRefreshTimeLimit are held, not acted on; X_ITE 16.6.0 reports bufferDuration -1 (not the UOM's 0) from the start while load is TRUE and nothing has loaded; the bridge does the same

CartoonVolumeStyle.note: X_ITE measures the angle against the direction eye to sample (not sample to eye), so the faces turned towards the eye are dropped and the far side of the cube shows; the bridge copies that (a convex cube looks the same either way); colorSteps 4 puts the 45 degree band exactly on a band edge, so it is not tested; the colours' alpha is not used

ChannelMerger.note: a child past the 32nd is not connected (as in X_ITE); adding or removing children at run time rebuilds the merger on the next tick; the merge of children that have more than one channel each (they are mixed down to one before the merger, a Web Audio rule) is not compared
ChannelMerger.prev_note: a child past the 32nd is not connected (as in X_ITE); adding or removing children at run time rebuilds the merger on the next tick

ChannelSelector.note: only two channels are exercised; a selection past the channels of the input gives silence in Web Audio (not tested)
ChannelSelector.prev_note: a disabled selector passes all channels (as in X_ITE); only the splitter size is checked, the routing of the chosen output is not read back

ChannelSplitter.note: a node past the 32nd in outputs is not connected (as in X_ITE); the splitter's own channel count (the number of nodes in outputs) is compared as a setting, the signal only for two outputs
ChannelSplitter.prev_note: a node past the 32nd in outputs is not connected (as in X_ITE); the wiring of each output to its node is not read back, only the splitter's size

Circle2D.note: lines are not pickable, so the check is the picture (silhouette overlap and the mean colour of the drawn pixels, SwiftShader CPU raster) plus the segment count between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs through its internal getVertices, a private API) and one line mesh in our body; line width is one pixel in both, ours is an anti-aliased ribbon
Circle2D.prev_note: lines are not pickable, so there is no hit probe: the segment count is compared between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs via its internal getVertices, which is a private API), and our body is checked to have built one line mesh; colour and line width are not compared

CollidableOffset.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 reads the translation and rotation of a CollidableOffset or CollidableShape only when the node first receives an event: a file that sets them and never touches them leaves the shape at the body origin so there it rests at 0.5 where the bridge rests at 1.5 (each engine is checked against its own value); the bridge applies them from the start; only translation and rotation of the offset are applied; the offset of an offset adds up

CollidableShape.note: box and sphere shapes are exact; cylinder and cone use their bounding sphere; indexed face sets and other geometry are not collided; a shape's own translation and rotation are used; enabled is read when the world is built

Collision.note: the group does nothing about collision: navigation never collides in the bridge, so isActive and collideTime never fire (X_ITE 16.6.0 fires them only when the navigation collides with the group); the proxy is held and not drawn

CollisionCollection.note: friction is one Coulomb coefficient for each contact (frictionCoefficients.x, or 0.5 when FRICTION_COEFFICIENT-2 is not applied); X_ITE 16.6.0 multiplies the two bodies' values, so it slides twice as far here (3.27 m against 1.63 m); X_ITE 16.6.0 sets a body's restitution only if the body's own speed is at least minBounceSpeed when the bounce is configured, and a fixed wall or ground has speed 0, so nothing bounces off it unless minBounceSpeed is 0 (the fixture sets 0); the bridge bounces when the speed of the contact reaches minBounceSpeed; X_ITE 16.6.0 only knows the appliedParameters spelling FRICTION_COEFFICIENT_2, the 4.0 XSD and spec say FRICTION_COEFFICIENT-2, so a valid scene never gets its friction in X_ITE; surfaceSpeed, slipFactors, softnessConstantForceMix, softnessErrorCorrection and the second friction value (rolling friction in Bullet) are kept and not used; collidables is kept and not used: bodies collide through their own geometry, as in X_ITE

CollisionSensor.note: isActive, intersections and contacts of an impact are not asserted: X_ITE sees an impact for one sub-step, the bridge for one of its 1/240 s steps; both are noisy; the events of one frame come in the order isActive, intersections, contacts (X_ITE: the same timestamp); the fixture reads values, not order; enabled is read only at load and when collider is written, as X_ITE 16.6.0 does; the specification says enabled switches the node

CollisionSpace.note: enabled and useGeometry are not read (X_ITE 16.6.0 does the same); the specification says they switch the space and select the geometry; the bounding box fields are kept and never used

ColorChaser.note: the intermediate values are pinned against X_ITE 16.6.0 as a curve: ours runs on a virtual clock (0.05 s steps), X_ITE on the real one (frames of about 17 ms), both measured from the isActive true event; every X_ITE sample must match ours interpolated within +-0.05 s of the same elapsed time; the worst difference is relative to the largest value on the curve (at least 1) and is bounded at 0.05: ours is interpolated linearly across the kink where the red channel saturates, which is most of the difference (colour path blue to red through magenta, checked sample by sample)
ColorChaser.prev_note: hue path between start and destination not pinned against X_ITE (end state only)

ColorDamper.note: the intermediate values are pinned against X_ITE 16.6.0 as a curve: ours runs on a virtual clock (0.05 s steps), X_ITE on the real one (frames of about 17 ms), both measured from the isActive true event; every X_ITE sample must match ours interpolated within +-0.05 s of the same elapsed time (bound 0.03); X_ITE 16.6.0 never reports isActive false when the hue path crosses the 0/1 seam; the curve itself agrees (documented in xiteDisagrees)
ColorDamper.prev_note: X_ITE 16.6.0 keeps isActive true after a hue-seam path (observed 7.3 s); ours stops. Intermediate colours not pinned

ComposedTexture3D.note: XSD finding: x3d-4.0.xsd writes the texture field of a ComposedTexture3D as an xs:sequence of ImageTexture, PixelTexture, MovieTexture, ProtoInstance repeated, not an xs:choice, so the slices must come in fours in that order and two ImageTextures do not validate; the fixture is checked against the XSD with that sequence made a choice (the receipt says so); the image field of a PixelTexture3D takes decimal numbers only in the XSD (no 0x hex); Babylon side: a WGSL ShaderMaterial over a RawTexture3D, shaded by the headlight (when NavigationInfo.headlight is TRUE) and by up to four lights that are on, as one-sided Lambert terms on the viewer-facing side; a spot light acts as a point light (no cone) and no light has attenuation, radius or global scope for a volume; the same shader as PixelTexture3D, compared there with X_ITE 16.6.0 on a lit box with a DirectionalLight and a PointLight (silhouette 0.95, mean abs diff 3.0 of 255, Chromium 153 SwiftShader); TextureProperties anisotropy and mipmaps are not applied to volumes
ComposedTexture3D.prev_note: XSD finding: x3d-4.0.xsd writes the texture field of a ComposedTexture3D as an xs:sequence of ImageTexture, PixelTexture, MovieTexture, ProtoInstance repeated, not an xs:choice, so the slices must come in fours in that order and two ImageTextures do not validate; the fixture is checked against the XSD with that sequence made a choice (the receipt says so); the image field of a PixelTexture3D takes decimal numbers only in the XSD (no 0x hex); Babylon side: a WGSL ShaderMaterial over a RawTexture3D, shaded by the headlight only (N dot view axis, two sided); other lights, TextureProperties anisotropy and mipmaps are not applied to volumes

ComposedVolumeStyle.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 and the bridge chain the styles (each replaces the colour it gets) where the specification text can be read as a sum; the bridge copies 16.6.0; only OpacityMapVolumeStyle, BlendedVolumeStyle, ProjectionVolumeStyle (dropped) and a nested Composed are tested here; the other styles use the same chain call; a Blended inside a Composed reads its second volume and the run-time changes of its texture rebuild the shader (BR.volr.touch walks the whole chain), not tested by picture

Contact.note: body1, body2, geometry1, geometry2: the bridge fills them, X_ITE leaves them null (checked on each side); the sign of contactNormal depends on the order of the pair and flips with nested shapes: only its length and axis are asserted; a Contact routed to set_contacts is held and does nothing, as in X_ITE

Contour2D.note: a Contour2D draws nothing by itself; what is compared is the run of u-v points a NurbsTrimmedSurface would read (X_ITE addTrimmingContour with no offset and unit scale, ours spec.contour), the list order and the add / remove rules

ContourPolyline2D.note: the node is data: nothing is drawn where it sits; the point list it gives to a Contour2D, a swung surface or a swept surface is what is compared, in both engines

Convolver.note: three channels, or more than four, are refused by Web Audio; the bridge keeps the previous response (X_ITE throws); the response is built at the audio context's own sample rate, as in X_ITE; the sample rate dependent numbers (the 10 ms delay) are taken from the page's audio context at run time; stereo and four channel responses are not compared with the signal, only the single channel one; numberOfChannels is a Convolver field in X_ITE 16.6.0 but is not in the X3D 4.0 UOM or XSD; the bridge has it as in X_ITE (set at run time only, since the XSD cannot write it)
Convolver.prev_note: three channels, or more than four, are refused by Web Audio; the bridge keeps the previous response (X_ITE throws); the response is built at the audio context's own sample rate, as in X_ITE; the processed sound is not compared; numberOfChannels is a Convolver field in X_ITE 16.6.0 but is not in the X3D 4.0 UOM or XSD; the bridge has it as in X_ITE (set at run time only, since the XSD cannot write it)

CoordinateChaser.note: the intermediate values are pinned against X_ITE 16.6.0 as a curve: ours runs on a virtual clock (0.05 s steps), X_ITE on the real one (frames of about 17 ms), both measured from the isActive true event; every X_ITE sample must match ours interpolated within +-0.05 s of the same elapsed time (bound 0.02, measured 0.003): list of 2 from the initial value, grown to 3 points, shrunk to 2; a list that changes length mid-chase restarts the chase at the new length with a new tail at 0; the end state (5 5 5, 6 6 6 after a change at 0.3 s) agrees with X_ITE, the frame of the change is not pinned
CoordinateChaser.prev_note: end state only; a list that changes length mid-chase restarts at the new length with the new tail at 0 (not compared with X_ITE)

CoordinateDamper.note: the intermediate values are pinned against X_ITE 16.6.0 as a curve: ours runs on a virtual clock (0.05 s steps), X_ITE on the real one (frames of about 17 ms), both measured from the isActive true event; every X_ITE sample must match ours interpolated within +-0.05 s of the same elapsed time (bound 0.02, measured 0.007): list of 2 from the initial value, grown to 3 points, shrunk to 2; a list that changes length mid-damping restarts at the new length with a new tail at 0; the end state agrees with X_ITE, the frame of the change is not pinned
CoordinateDamper.prev_note: end state only; a list that changes length mid-chase restarts at the new length with the new tail at 0 (not compared with X_ITE)

CoordinateDouble.note: the points are kept as 32-bit floats (the geometry code reads Float32Array); doubles finer than about 7 digits or larger than 3e38 are not kept; only the triangle positions are compared with X_ITE (pointer hit and miss), not shading
CoordinateDouble.prev_note: the points are kept as 32-bit floats (the geometry code reads Float32Array); doubles finer than about 7 digits or larger than 3e38 are not kept; only the triangle positions are compared with X_ITE (pointer hit and miss), not shading

CylinderSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 numerically: trackPoint_changed and rotation_changed in cylinder mode (off-axis press), in disk mode (axisRotation turns the axis to the view direction) and with minAngle/maxAngle; rotations compared as quaternions (X_ITE writes the same turn with the axis flipped and the angle negated); unlike X_ITE the angle accumulates past a half turn (X_ITE returns a rotation of at most 180 degrees, so a full drag around the axis jumps back); a deliberate difference, quality over match; isOver is picked once per animation frame and keeps its value while a drag is active
CylinderSensor.prev_note: disk mode (view along the axis) is implemented but only the cylinder mode is compared with X_ITE; trackPoint_changed not compared

DISEntityManager.note: no entity is ever added or removed: the manager does not listen for ESPDUs, and nothing here can be tested without a network; the mapping children are held and never drawn

DISEntityTypeMapping.note: the url is held and never fetched (X_ITE measured 0 requests; the bridge issues none either); a mapping can never be resolved because no entity is ever received; autoRefresh never fires

Delay.note: Web Audio takes a maximum above 0 and below 180 s; X_ITE throws outside that, the bridge holds maxDelayTime to 0.001..179.999 (not tested, since X_ITE cannot be asked)
Delay.prev_note: Web Audio takes a maximum above 0 and below 180 s; X_ITE throws outside that, the bridge holds maxDelayTime to 0.001..179.999 (not tested, since X_ITE cannot be asked)

DirectionalLight.note: shadows and shadowIntensity are read and not used (no shadow generator is made); ambientIntensity feeds Babylon's one scene ambient colour (the sum over the lights that are on, times material ambientIntensity * diffuseColor, compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in the picture, mad 1.6); a light with global FALSE adds its ambient to every shape, not only its group; global FALSE lights the meshes below the parent group; meshes added later are picked up when the mesh count changes (checked in our body)
DirectionalLight.prev_note: ambientIntensity is not used (no ambient term in the Babylon light); shadows are not made; global FALSE lights the meshes below the parent group; meshes added later are picked up when the mesh count changes (checked in our body, X_ITE draws the same picture)

Disk2D.note: the circle is a 96 segment polygon (X_ITE 16.6.0 uses its own polygon): silhouettes agree to about a pixel in the picture, not vertex for vertex; the texture coordinates are planar (the disk mapped on the unit square); they are not compared with X_ITE

DoubleAxisHingeJoint.note: the bridge builds the hinge-2 joint (anchors meet, the axes stay at 90 degrees, a motor and limit on each); X_ITE 16.6.0 builds a plain btHingeConstraint about axis1, so axis2 does nothing there; desiredAngularVelocity1 and 2 with maxTorque1 and 2 turn the hinges in the bridge; X_ITE ignores them; suspensionForce and suspensionErrorCorrection are kept and not used

DynamicsCompressor.note: the compressor's time response (attack and release as a function of time) is not compared, only the settled level; Web Audio's compressor adds a makeup gain and a look-ahead of about 6 ms that no X3D field controls; the reduction output is read once per frame (3 frames per second in our reader)
DynamicsCompressor.prev_note: reduction is read from the audio node every tick while active; with real sound it follows the signal, here only silence is tested

EdgeEnhancementVolumeStyle.note: a flat region has no gradient and is dropped, so a constant volume draws nothing with this style (tested in the Silhouette fixture); edgeColor's alpha is not used; edgeColor mixing needs a normal that is not along the view axis; it is covered by the formula and the rotated-view test is left to the next batch

EspduTransform.note: the bridge copies X_ITE: translation, rotation, scale, center, scaleOrientation of an EspduTransform are not applied (the specification says they place the entity like a Transform); no dead reckoning, no network (isStandAlone never fires), no articulation parameters; the DIS traffic cannot be tested from a scene file; bboxDisplay draws no wire cube in the bridge (no shared bbox helper yet); X_ITE draws one

ExplosionEmitter.note: colour is compared: a quad particle is lit like a surface (emissive + diffuse x headlight, white for this Material); ours is 255 white, X_ITE 16.6.0's mean over its drawn pixels is about 200 (its edges are blended), fg tolerance 70; no fade at the end of life without a colorRamp (as X_ITE); particle age at the shot differs between the engines on this CPU raster (ours runs on elapsed time at about 3 frames per second under SwiftShader), so the extent is compared with a wide bound and the speed is checked from the particle list in our body
ExplosionEmitter.prev_note: particle age at the shot differs between the engines on this CPU raster (ours runs on elapsed time at about 3 frames per second under SwiftShader), so the extent is compared with a wide bound and the speed is checked from the particle list in our body; X_ITE 16.6.0 draws the particles white on this raster, ours uses the Material emissive colour (colour is not compared); the X_ITE picture also shows a swirl pattern that ours does not reproduce

Extrusion.note: compared in the picture by silhouette and mean colour (SwiftShader CPU raster); creaseAngle smoothing, texture coordinates of the caps and degenerate frames (a spine that doubles back, collinear spine points) are not compared with X_ITE

FillProperties.note: a shape with filled=false and hatched=false is not drawn but still answers the pointer, as in X_ITE 16.6.0 (the 4.0 text does not say); compared by pointer-over probes; the 19 hatch patterns are drawn in screen space, one texel per pixel, like X_ITE 16.6.0 (the masks are derived from its hatching images); compared in the picture with styles 3, 6, 12 and 17 (silhouette 0.96, mean abs diff 1.8 of 255 on SwiftShader); the pixel scale of a high-density screen is not read (scale 1)
FillProperties.prev_note: a shape with filled=false and hatched=false is not drawn but still answers the pointer, as in X_ITE 16.6.0 (the 4.0 text does not say); compared by pointer-over probes (hidden fill is not hit, hatched and plain fills are) and, in our body only, the hatch overlay mesh; line pattern, thickness and screen-space scaling are not compared with X_ITE; hatchStyle 7 to 19 are drawn as style 6; the pattern follows the geometry's texture coordinates, a geometry without them shows no hatch

FogCoordinate.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in the picture (silhouette 1.0, mean abs diff 1.1 of 255, Chromium 153 SwiftShader); only IndexedTriangleSet and the bridged geometry sets take a fogCoord; IndexedFaceSet and the others the stock reader draws do not have the field; the fog is a second copy of the mesh drawn over the first with vertex alpha = depth, so it blends after the surface is tone mapped (X_ITE blends inside the shader); vertices past the end of depth read as 0 (clear); the world Fog is new to the bridge (stock body never drew it): it fogs every mesh no LocalFog covers; all fogs share the fog law of the first active one
FogCoordinate.prev_note: only IndexedTriangleSet and the bridged geometry sets take a fogCoord; IndexedFaceSet and the others the stock reader draws do not have the field; the fog is a second copy of the mesh drawn over the first with vertex alpha = depth, so it blends after the surface is tone mapped (X_ITE blends inside the shader); vertices past the end of depth read as 0 (clear); the world Fog is new to the bridge (stock body never drew it): it fogs every mesh no LocalFog covers; all fogs share the fog law of the first active one

Gain.note: a Gain has no Web Audio node of its own beyond the input stage (as in X_ITE); channelCount, channelCountMode and channelInterpretation are compared as settings, not as a channel mix with a multichannel signal (the ChannelMerger test does that)
Gain.prev_note: a Gain has no Web Audio node of its own beyond the input stage (as in X_ITE)

GeneratedCubeMapTexture.note: measured against X_ITE 16.6.0 on a mirrored ball with face colours (Chromium 153 SwiftShader): the three visible face patches sit at the same places, silhouette overlap 0.73, mean abs diff 2.2 of 255; ours draws the top (blue) patch taller; not closed; the faces of the cube are not turned like X_ITE's (flat colours cannot show it); the picture is taken from the origin of the ball in world space, not in the camera space of X_ITE's cube; the probe renders meshes as they are: it does not draw the Background spheres of other layers
GeneratedCubeMapTexture.prev_note: the faces of the cube are not turned like X_ITE's (flat colours cannot show it); the picture is taken from the origin of the ball in world space, not in the camera space of X_ITE's cube; the probe renders meshes as they are: it does not draw the Background spheres of other layers

GeoCoordinate.note: the geometry reads the converted points; set1Point and the inverse of the conversion are not reachable from a scene file; UTM and GC are checked in the unit maths of the bridge (BR.geo, numbers from X_ITE) not by picture

GeoElevationGrid.note: the grid is drawn per triangle with the unweighted normals of X_ITE (the average depends on the triangulation); only the facets and the smooth ridge pixels are tested; set_height is checked in the interpolation fixture style (an event) and not drawn here; tangent is not made (X_ITE builds it for normal maps; the bridge draws no normal maps from it)

GeoLOD.note: children are fetched at first entry to level 1 and never unloaded: the "fetched once" rule is not counted in the fixture; level_changed before children is the order in X_ITE and in the bridge; the fixture does not assert event order (the runner reads values); the root is kept on screen until all four children are finished, so a slow child delays the picture, not level_changed (not tested: data: urls arrive at once); bboxDisplay and the bounding box of a GeoLOD are not implemented

GeoLocation.note: the placement matrices of the geocentric (no origin) cases are checked in our node only: X_ITE has no way to read them back, the picture tests use the rotateYUp origin; the node drawn is a Babylon TransformNode, whose world matrix is 32 bit: without a GeoOrigin a point 6.4e6 m from the centre of the earth is only good to about half a metre in the picture

GeoMetadata.note: the url is held, never fetched (X_ITE requests nothing either); summary keywords are not interpreted; nothing here can show that no request left the page: the bridge has no fetch in the node, checked by reading the code

GeoOrigin.note: only GD and UTM and GC geoSystems with the WE and IN style ellipsoids are exercised in the unit checks of BR.geo; the picture tests use GD WE; a plain list handed to a double field of X_ITE 16.6.0 (a harness slip, now converted to SFVec3d) turns the picture to nothing and a second set kills the page; the origin is read at use: a change of geoSystem of an existing GeoOrigin at run time is not tested (the field is initializeOnly)

GeoPositionInterpolator.note: when a key sits on the GeoOrigin its local vector is zero and both engines give the same odd point (lon 7.04, 88.5 km below the ellipsoid at the middle of 0 to 20 degrees): the case is kept because the two agree; the great-circle path pivoting on the GeoOrigin is X_ITE's own choice (a defect against any sane reading); the bridge copies it so the numbers agree; the interpolation is not linear in latitude, longitude and height, which a reader of the specification may expect; UTM keys are not tested here: the unit maths of the bridge covers UTM, the interpolator uses the same conversion

GeoProximitySensor.note: a sensor inside a Transform reports geoCoord_changed of the local position (X_ITE's shortcut), not the viewer's geographic position; X_ITE sends isActive false and exitTime twice when the sensor is disabled while active: the bridge sends them once (the fixture asserts at least one); the viewer's own navigation (mouse, keys) is not simulated: the camera is moved by writing the Viewpoint position; events carry the pose of the camera in the same frame (no frame of lag as in X_ITE)

GeoTouchSensor.note: hitGeoCoord under a Transform or GeoLocation is wrong on purpose (X_ITE converts the local point as if it were in the GeoOrigin frame); the specification wants the true position of the hit; the bridge reports a click as one press and release (isActive true then false, touchTime); the hit outputs are sent again after it, X_ITE sends them after press and release too; hitPoint repeats with every pointer move in X_ITE, once per move here; hover events repeat on every pointer move in both engines; the fixture checks values, not counts

GeoTransform.note: a scale under a non-zero scaleOrientation that is not uniform is a shear, which the node cannot hold (dropped, noted by the body); the matrix is computed in double precision, drawn through a 32 bit Babylon world matrix

GeoViewpoint.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 and the 4.0 schema have no set_position, set_orientation, position_changed, geoCoord, elevationScale or navType on GeoViewpoint: none is implemented; navigation does not write `position`; the speed is computed, not used by a navigation mode in this bridge; near 0.125 and far 1e9 as in X_ITE: with Babylon's depth buffer the far range costs precision at long distances (X_ITE draws the GeoViewpoint with a logarithmic depth buffer)

HAnimDisplacer.note: a vertex weighted over several joints is displaced before skinning (Babylon MorphTarget, the glTF order); X_ITE 16.6.0 adds joint rotation * (displacement * weight) after skinning with the rotation of the displacer's joint alone: identical (<= 1e-7 on the rig) for a vertex that follows the displacer's joint alone and at the rest pose, 0.053 (weight 0.5) to 0.106 (weight 1) world units apart on the half J0 / half J1 ring of this fixture for a 0.3 unit displacement in the 45 degree pose; a displacer on a segment moves the segment's own vertices in the segment's frame; X_ITE 16.6.0 rotates the displacement by the segment's matrix in the humanoid's frame and the shape's own transform rotates it again, so a bent segment collapses to a sliver there (see the bent shot); the bridge draws the intended rectangle

HAnimHumanoid.note: skinNormal, skinBindingCoords and skinBindingNormals are stored; neither engine uses them (X_ITE 16.6.0 reads skinCoord only): the skin normals follow the bone matrices in the shader (X_ITE blends the inverse transpose per joint, the same for rotations, different under non-uniform joint scale); only IndexedFaceSet and IndexedTriangleSet skin shapes are skinned (a vertex's coordinate index is known); a vertex with more than 8 joint influences keeps the 8 largest, X_ITE has no limit; the viewpoints, joints, segments and sites lists are references (not drawn twice)

HAnimJoint.note: llimit, ulimit, limitOrientation and stiffness are stored and routed but limit nothing: neither engine solves joint limits (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not either)

HAnimSegment.note: mass, centerOfMass and momentsOfInertia are stored and routed, no engine uses them (physics belongs to the RigidBodyPhysics group)

HAnimSite.note: a Viewpoint inside a site of the humanoid's viewpoints list is not bound from the site in the bridge (the site is a Transform; HAnim viewpoints are not navigation viewpoints)

ImageCubeMapTexture.note: measured against X_ITE 16.6.0 on a mirrored ball with six flat face colours (Chromium 153 SwiftShader): silhouette overlap 0.99 and mean abs diff 10.4 of 255 over the ball region (0.87 and 15.9 over the whole frame, which holds the X_ITE badge), the six face colours land at the same places (pixel probes) but our face borders are soft and curved differently from X_ITE's hard diagonal borders (Babylon samples the cube per pixel with a linear filter, X_ITE per vertex coordinate); not closed; the Material is added to the reflection, not multiplied with it; the reflection is of the world (it does not turn with the camera as CAMERASPACEREFLECTIONVECTOR does in X_ITE); flat face colours cannot show if the face images are turned like X_ITE's; a 2:1 panorama is converted but its orientation is not compared; KTX2 and DDS are not read
ImageCubeMapTexture.prev_note: the Material is added to the reflection, not multiplied with it; the reflection is of the world (it does not turn with the camera as CAMERASPACEREFLECTIONVECTOR does in X_ITE); flat face colours cannot show if the face images are turned like X_ITE's; a 2:1 panorama is converted but its orientation is not compared; KTX2 and DDS are not read

ImageTexture3D.note: the DDS volume (right) is drawn by ours and shown white by X_ITE 16.6.0 on this raster (Suspected: its DDS 3D reader does not take this uncompressed RGBA header); the picture comparison covers the NRRD volume (left); ImageTexture3D reads uncompressed DDS volumes and uchar NRRD (raw, gzip, ascii); DICOM and compressed DDS are not read; the volume shader is shared with PixelTexture3D and ComposedTexture3D: lit by the headlight and up to four lights (checked on PixelTexture3D against X_ITE 16.6.0, mean abs diff 3.0 of 255)
ImageTexture3D.prev_note: the DDS volume (right) is drawn by ours and shown white by X_ITE 16.6.0 on this raster (Suspected: its DDS 3D reader does not take this uncompressed RGBA header); the picture comparison covers the NRRD volume (left); ImageTexture3D reads uncompressed DDS volumes and uchar NRRD (raw, gzip, ascii); DICOM and compressed DDS are not read

IndexedQuadSet.note: attrib is read and kept; only a shader program would consume it, and no shader language runs in the bridge (see ShaderProgram, ProgramShader)

IndexedTriangleFanSet.note: attrib is read and kept; only a shader program would consume it, and no shader language runs in the bridge (see ShaderProgram, ProgramShader)

IndexedTriangleStripSet.note: attrib is read and kept; only a shader program would consume it, and no shader language runs in the bridge (see ShaderProgram, ProgramShader)

IsoSurfaceVolumeData.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 draws the 'surface' as every sample above the value (a first-hit march), flat grey and unlit unless a renderStyle is given; contourStepSize with a surface value is not applied: X_ITE 16.6.0 tests only the lowest contour of its generated list, which is not the specification's meaning, so the bridge leaves the field kept and unused; the voxels and gradients events after load are honoured by the bridge, ignored by X_ITE

KeySensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 event for event: Shift, Control and Alt flags, character keys, Enter, F1 and F12, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown and the four arrows (action codes 13-20), two keys held at once (isActive until the first release, as X_ITE), key repeat (a second keyDown raises keyPress again), enabled false; key events come from the focused canvas only (keydown and keyup, as in X_ITE); a page that keeps focus elsewhere must focus the canvas
KeySensor.prev_note: Alt/Control flags follow the Shift path but were only tested with Shift; key repeat while a key is held fires keyPress again, as in the browser

Layer.note: viewport of a Layer is a clip rectangle of the layer's camera, compared with X_ITE in the Viewport fixture, not here; a pick sensor sees only the shapes of its own layer (X_ITE gives every layer a pickable group of its own); the world counts as layer 0; a layer's pointer events: the top drawn layer that has a hit wins whatever its depth; compared on the LayerSet fixture
Layer.prev_note: pickable, objectType, pointerEvents and viewport are held: picking does not respect layers; addChildren and removeChildren rebuild the layer; this is checked in the SAI test of LayerSet only if the engine exposes them (X_ITE does), here only the fields are compared

LayerSet.note: activeLayer (which layer the user navigates) and the navigation of a layer's own Viewpoint are held, not acted on: the user always navigates the world's camera; a layer's Viewpoint is read once and per frame, not bound or animated; the layer has no NavigationInfo, Background or headlight of its own; lights of the world light the meshes of every layer; a layer has no lights of its own; order without any visible layer draws the world (Babylon needs a camera)

Layout.note: three pictures (settings of all six fields) agree with X_ITE 16.6.0: silhouette iou 1.0, mean difference 1.2 of 255 on Chromium 153.0.8010.12 SwiftShader / Babylon 9.32.0; a Layout inside a LayoutGroup that sits in the perspective world uses the near plane of the camera as the viewport size (as X_ITE does), so only the orthographic layer is probed; the offset and size units of PIXEL count CSS pixels of the canvas; no device pixel ratio is read (X_ITE divides by its ContentScale)
Layout.prev_note: a Layout inside a LayoutGroup that sits in the perspective world uses the near plane of the camera as the viewport size (like X_ITE); only the orthographic layer is probed here; the offset and size units of PIXEL count CSS pixels of the canvas; no device pixel ratio is read

LayoutGroup.note: viewport of a LayoutGroup is held: the world camera is shared with the rest of the scene; a LayoutGroup in the perspective world uses the near plane of the camera as the viewport size, so its layout is microscopic there, as in X_ITE; only the orthographic layer is probed; XSD finding: x3d-4.0.xsd (x3d_mcp) lists LayoutGroup only in the pick-target content model, in no child content model, so NO scene can hold a LayoutGroup and still validate; the fixture is checked against the XSD plus one line (receipt names it)

LayoutLayer.note: pickable and objectType gate a pick sensor in the layer, pointerEvents gates a TouchSensor in it, addChildren / removeChildren change what it draws (all compared with X_ITE 16.6.0); two pictures of the layer's viewport (left and right half) agree with X_ITE 16.6.0: silhouette iou 1.0, mean difference 1.5 of 255 on Chromium 153.0.8010.12 SwiftShader / Babylon 9.32.0; a LayoutLayer without a Layout shows its children as they are; a Layout is probed in the Layout fixture
LayoutLayer.prev_note: pickable, objectType and pointerEvents are held: picking does not respect layers; a LayoutLayer without a Layout shows its children as they are, a Layout is probed in the Layout fixture

LinePickSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in scene mode: sensors in a Transform with a Shape sibling (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not traverse a group that holds only a pick sensor, so the fixtures add a 0.02 unit Box beside each sensor); two segments through a Box and a Sphere: pickedGeometry, pickedPoint and pickedNormal compared as sets, BOUNDS and GEOMETRY; pickedPoint, pickedNormal agree within 0.02: Babylon's Sphere is tessellated differently from X_ITE's (points on the sphere differ by up to 1 percent); pickedTextureCoordinate is filled from the mesh UVs and not compared (box UV layouts differ between the engines); pickedPoint is in the target's own coordinates (as X_ITE 16.6.0)

LineSet.note: normal, fogCoord and attrib are read and ignored; line colour: the drawn pixels are about 20 percent brighter than X_ITE's one pixel lines in the picture (mean colour 60,120,61 against 48,99,51), the anti-aliased ribbon covers more pixels than a raw GL line
LineSet.prev_note: lines are not pickable, so there is no hit probe: the segment count is compared between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs via its internal getVertices, which is a private API), and our body is checked to have built one line mesh; colour and line width are not compared; normal, fogCoord and attrib are read and ignored

ListenerPointSource.note: the listener follows the node once per frame; X_ITE does it while it draws the node; enabled = false leaves the listener where it was; interauralDistance and dopplerEnabled are held, Web Audio has no use for them; the 4.0 UOM gives ListenerPointSource gain, mediaDeviceID and a start/stop clock; X_ITE 16.6.0 has none of them, so they are held here and not compared
ListenerPointSource.prev_note: the listener follows the node once per frame; X_ITE does it while it draws the node; enabled = false leaves the listener where it was; interauralDistance and dopplerEnabled are held, Web Audio has no use for them; the 4.0 UOM gives ListenerPointSource gain, mediaDeviceID and a start/stop clock; X_ITE 16.6.0 has none of them, so they are held here and not compared

LoadSensor.note: Inline, audio and movie children are fetched, not decoded: loaded means the url answered; only the first working url of a child is used; X_ITE 16.6.0 hands the world over only after every resource has loaded, so the in-flight timeOut state (aborted, not yet loaded) can only be checked in our reader; the end state is compared; a change of children or enabled true restarts the count as in X_ITE 16.6.0; a child that loaded before counts at once
LoadSensor.prev_note: a change of children after load does not restart the count (X_ITE restarts); Inline, audio and movie children are fetched, not decoded: loaded means the url answered; only the first working url of a child is used; X_ITE 16.6.0 hands the world over only after every resource has loaded, so the in-flight timeOut state (aborted, not yet loaded) can only be checked in our reader; the end state is compared

LocalFog.note: LINEAR fog compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in the picture (silhouette 0.97, mean abs diff 1.9 of 255, Chromium 153 SwiftShader); the EXPONENTIAL laws below are checked in our body only; EXPONENTIAL and EXPONENTIAL2 use Babylon's EXP and EXP2 scaled to 1/e at half the range: close to X3D's exp(-d/(range-d)) in the first half, softer at the end (X3D reaches full fog at the range); all LocalFogs of a world share the fog law of the first active one (Babylon picks the law per scene, not per mesh); colour and range are per scope; the range is not scaled by the parent's transform scale, X3D measures it in the LocalFog's own coordinate system; two meshes sharing one Babylon material would share the fog parameters of whichever draws first; the body makes one material per shape, so it does not happen here
LocalFog.prev_note: EXPONENTIAL and EXPONENTIAL2 use Babylon's EXP and EXP2 scaled to 1/e at half the range: close to X3D's exp(-d/(range-d)) in the first half, softer at the end (X3D reaches full fog at the range); all LocalFogs of a world share the fog law of the first active one (Babylon picks the law per scene, not per mesh); colour and range are per scope; the range is not scaled by the parent's transform scale, X3D measures it in the LocalFog's own coordinate system; two meshes sharing one Babylon material would share the fog parameters of whichever draws first; the body makes one material per shape, so it does not happen here

Matrix3VertexAttribute.note: the matrices are attributes for a shader program; the bridge has none (WGSL ports only), so nothing is drawn from them

Matrix4VertexAttribute.note: the matrices are attributes for a shader program; the bridge has none (WGSL ports only), so nothing is drawn from them

MicrophoneSource.note: the test browser has a fake capture device, not a real microphone, so which physical device a real mediaDeviceID reaches and the permission prompt are not compared; the browser's own capture processing (echo cancellation, gain control) is whatever the browser applies to both engines; streamIdentifier is held (X_ITE lists it, the 4.0 UOM does not for this node)
MicrophoneSource.prev_note: getUserMedia is not tested (no device, no permission prompt in the test browser); streamIdentifier is held; X_ITE lists it, the 4.0 UOM does not for this node

MotorJoint.note: the bridge applies axisNTorque about motorNAxis (fixed in body 1) on body 2 and the opposite on body 1 for the first enabledAxes axes; autoCalc and the stop bounce and error correction fields are kept and not used; motorNAngle is the signed twist of body 2 about each axis; X_ITE 16.6.0 has no motor at all

MovieTexture.note: timing is compared through the fields only; the picture on the box is not compared with X_ITE; the clip is played muted (a page may not start sound by itself); gain and pitch are read and not used; a loop and a natural end are not exercised by the test

MultiTexture.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in the picture (silhouette 0.97, mean abs diff 1.6 of 255 on SwiftShader) for MODULATE (red x green = black) and ADD (red + green = yellow); function, source, color and alpha are read and not used; modes other than REPLACE, MODULATE, MODULATE2X, MODULATE4X and ADD are drawn as MODULATE; the combine is made once on a 256 x 256 canvas: it does not follow the lighting or the vertex colour; a small image is magnified with hard texels like X_ITE
MultiTexture.prev_note: X_ITE is compared on loading and drawing the shapes; the combined colour is checked in our body only (red x green = black for MODULATE, red + green = yellow for ADD); function, source, color and alpha are read and not used; modes other than REPLACE, MODULATE, MODULATE2X, MODULATE4X and ADD are drawn as MODULATE; the combine is made once on a 256 x 256 canvas: it does not follow the lighting or the vertex colour

MultiTextureCoordinate.note: the picture is made once, in the first channel's coordinates; channel i is carried as the affine map that takes channel 0 to channel i (least squares over the vertices): exact for a quad or any planar mapping, the nearest affine map otherwise (noted on the page); the X3D 4.0 use of a MultiTextureCoordinate, where a material names a channel by its `mapping`, is the Library hall port's (hall/body-hl.js) and is not part of the bridge body

MultiTextureTransform.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in the picture (silhouette 0.97, mean abs diff 3.2 of 255 on SwiftShader): the shifted box swaps the halves in both; only MultiTexture stages are moved; a plain TextureTransform on a single texture is applied by the Material path (bridged), not by the unlit one; edits to the transform after the build are not followed
MultiTextureTransform.prev_note: X_ITE is compared on loading and drawing the shapes; the shifted colours are checked in our body only (red|blue image shifted by half a tile swaps the halves); only MultiTexture stages are moved; a plain TextureTransform on a single texture is not applied by the stock body (TextureTransform stays 'base'); edits to the transform after the build are not followed

NurbsCurve.note: weights: X_ITE 16.6.0 draws a weighted curve with the weights applied wrongly (a quarter circle of radius up to 1.24); this node follows the standard (radius 1 to 1e-5), so a weighted curve is only checked in this engine and X_ITE only records its own measure; line width is one pixel in both engines (the body draws an anti-aliased ribbon of the same width); the control points are Coordinate or CoordinateDouble; GeoCoordinate is not read as a control point

NurbsCurve2D.note: weights: X_ITE 16.6.0 gives a weighted curve the radius 1.24 where a rational B-spline has 1.00 (the weights are not applied as homogeneous coordinates); this node follows the standard, the quarter circle is exact to 1e-5; tessellate(type) is the node's own reading; a trimmed surface (NurbsTrimmedSurface, a later batch) is what draws a contour

NurbsOrientationInterpolator.note: weights: the direction of a weighted curve is the derivative of the rational curve here; X_ITE 16.6.0 ignores the weights, so for a weighted curve only this engine is checked (against the exact circle tangent); a curve with zero derivative at the fraction (all control points equal, a stopped point) raises no event here; X_ITE normalises a zero vector (undefined)

NurbsPatchSurface.note: normals: this node draws the analytic normal dS/du x dS/dv at every grid point; X_ITE 16.6.0 averages face normals inside an 85 degree crease, so at low tessellation its shading is faceted where ours is smooth (measured largest component difference 0.21 at 12 x 12 cells and 0.28 at 8 x 8, compared at 0.3); weights: X_ITE 16.6.0 does not apply them as a rational surface needs (the quarter cylinder reaches radius 1.24); this node follows the standard (radius 1 to 1e-5), checked in this engine only; solid FALSE seen from behind: X_ITE 16.6.0 lights the back face, the Babylon body draws a counter-clockwise face seen from behind black (the same for an IndexedFaceSet with solid FALSE, measured in a two-quad fixture: 9312 against 19012 drawn pixels); the patch P6 is therefore off screen and only its triangles are compared; a closed surface (uClosed): positions, texture coordinates and the triangles agree with X_ITE; the shading is smooth across the seam here, X_ITE leaves a seam in its normals (its own source says "TODO: handle uClosed"); NurbsTextureCoordinate as texCoord is a later batch (a TextureCoordinate with one point per control point is supported and compared)

NurbsPositionInterpolator.note: weights: X_ITE 16.6.0 returns the unweighted B-spline point (0.75, 0.75, 0) where a rational B-spline has (0.7071, 0.7071, 0); this node follows the standard (the weighted quarter circle is exact to 1e-6); the curve is open (the node has no closed field): a closed loop needs its own start point repeated and ends on it; X_ITE 16.6.0 throws TypeError (reading domain of undefined) when set_fraction reaches an interpolator whose curve is invalid (order 4 with three control points) and the page stops answering; the bridge raises no event, so that case is only sent to this engine

NurbsSet.note: a scale of 0 or below leaves X_ITE 16.6.0 with 0 segments (NaN vertices); here the surface keeps one cell; the set draws nothing itself in either engine: the surfaces are drawn by the Shapes that hold them; bboxSize / bboxCenter / bboxDisplay / visible are kept as field values and do not move anything (X_ITE 16.6.0 uses the bbox of the surfaces for culling only); NurbsTrimmedSurface (a later batch) joins the set the same way (the scale code names it already)

NurbsSurfaceInterpolator.note: weights: X_ITE 16.6.0 leaves the weights out of position_changed (0.75, 0.75, 0.25 at the middle of the quarter cylinder; the exact value is 0.7071, 0.7071, 0.25); this node follows the standard; normal_changed is a unit vector here; X_ITE 16.6.0 sends the cross product dS/du x dS/dv (same direction, the length of the cross product); the directions agree to 1e-5 and are what is compared; the surface is open (no uClosed / vClosed on the node)

NurbsSweptSurface.note: the frame at an interior spine point: this node (like the swung surface and the Library hall Extrusion) takes the Y axis along the chord spine[i+1] - spine[i-1]; X_ITE 16.6.0 takes the bisector of the two unit vectors; they agree for an evenly spaced spine and differ slightly (compared at 0.02) for a bent one; solid FALSE seen from behind: X_ITE 16.6.0 lights the back face, the Babylon body draws it black (the same gap as the patch and the swung surface); the two sided surface here is seen from the front; no scale, orientation or caps (an Extrusion's, not this node's); texture coordinates run 0..1 along the cross-section (s) and the trajectory (t)

NurbsSwungSurface.note: the frame at an interior spine point: this node (like the Library hall Extrusion) takes the Y axis along the chord spine[i+1] - spine[i-1], which is how the standard words it (Likely: read from memory of 19775-1 13.3.5, the text itself is not in the repository); X_ITE 16.6.0 takes the bisector of the two unit vectors. The two are the same for an evenly spaced spine (octagon trajectory: 1.2e-7) and differ by up to 0.017 in the 2.2 unit vase whose spine points are unevenly spaced (compared at 0.02); solid FALSE seen from behind: X_ITE 16.6.0 lights the back face, the Babylon body draws it black (the same gap as the patch and IndexedFaceSet); the two sided swung surface here is seen from the front; no scale, orientation or caps (the NURBS nodes have none); texture coordinates run 0..1 along the profile (s) and the trajectory (t), the same numbers as X_ITE; the normals are smoothed over every shared vertex (crease angle pi, as X_ITE sets it): the shading agrees in the pictures (mean colour within 10 of 255, picture difference about 3 of 255), not per vertex

NurbsTextureCoordinate.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 samples the texture surface with haveWeights false, so the weight field of a NurbsTextureCoordinate does nothing (the texture coordinates are the plain B-spline of the control points); the standard calls it rational; the bridge does what X_ITE does and the fixture asserts X_ITE's numbers; the tessellation of the texture surface is the surface's own (one grid): a texture surface is sampled at the same fractions of its own domain as the patch

NurbsTrimmedSurface.note: the trimmed surface is compared by the area and the bounding box of the triangles that are kept (the two engines cut the grid into different triangles at the contour, so triangle corners are not compared); the picture is compared by silhouette and mean colour; a contour that crosses itself, or two contours that cross each other, is cut by parity in both engines but the bridge was only tested with contours that do not cross; the new corners take position, normal and texture coordinate from the grid triangle they fall in, as X_ITE does, so the cut edge is a polyline of the contour lying on the grid's flat triangles

OpacityMapVolumeStyle.note: the 4.0 XSD lacks transferFunction in its containerField enumeration (the fixture is checked against a copy that has it); only a PixelTexture is read as a 2D transfer function (an ImageTexture is not: the white texel stands in); a 3D transfer function (PixelTexture3D, ComposedTexture3D, ImageTexture3D) is read as X_ITE does, at (r, r, r); X_ITE reads the table at (r, g) of the colour the default ramp already made, which is (r, r): the spec's intensity against gradient is not what 16.6.0 does and the bridge copies 16.6.0; a changed transfer function picture is taken up by the bridge and not by X_ITE 16.6.0 (measured: a PixelTexture image written after load changes nothing there, a toggle of enabled does not help); the 2D transfer function repeats in X_ITE unless repeatS and repeatT are false: voxel 255 then lands on texel 0 (the fixture sets repeatS and repeatT to false)

OrientationChaser.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

OrientationDamper.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

OrthoViewpoint.note: three pictures (default view, a wider fieldOfView, a shifted position) agree with X_ITE 16.6.0: silhouette iou 1.0 and mean difference 0.4 to 1.4 of 255 on Chromium 153.0.8010.12 SwiftShader / Babylon 9.32.0; the bound is iou 0.99, mad 3; a bind between an OrthoViewpoint and another viewpoint is a cut here (the fixture uses transitionType TELEPORT in both engines): no fly-through is drawn between a perspective and an orthographic view; the user's mouse wheel scales the area and the drag pans in view units; X_ITE's fieldOfViewOffset / fieldOfViewScale animations and viewAll are not modelled; near and far default to 0.1 and 10000 when nearDistance or farDistance is not positive (X_ITE takes the navigation avatar size for near)
OrthoViewpoint.prev_note: a bind between an OrthoViewpoint and another viewpoint is a cut: no fly-through is drawn; the user's mouse wheel scales the area, the drag pans in view units; X_ITE's fieldOfViewOffset / fieldOfViewScale animations and viewAll are not modelled; near and far default to 0.1 and 10000 when nearDistance or farDistance is not positive (X_ITE takes the navigation avatar size for near)

OscillatorSource.note: pause stops the tone (30 ms fade) and resume starts a new one, as in X_ITE; the four extra OscillatorSources are only there to hold the waves for the test; the tone is measured by rms, frequency and harmonic amplitude (Hann window, exact frequency), not sample by sample, because the two engines run on separate real time audio clocks; the exact phase and the start instant (which follows the 3 frames per second of the rig in our reader) are not compared
OscillatorSource.prev_note: pause stops the tone (30 ms fade) and resume starts a new one, as in X_ITE; the four extra OscillatorSources are only there to hold the waves for the test

PackagedShader.note: no shader language runs: the node is only a holder (the WebGPU body runs WGSL ports of known GLSL parts); author-defined <field> declarations are not read for this node (the stock reader reads them for ComposedShader only)

PeriodicWave.note: the wave only sounds through an OscillatorSource; disableNormalization is not a field of this node in X3D 4.0 (Web Audio normalises, as in X_ITE)
PeriodicWave.prev_note: the waveform is only used through an OscillatorSource; the type to wave-type mapping is tested there

PickableGroup.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in scene mode: sensors in a Transform with a Shape sibling (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not traverse a group that holds only a pick sensor, so the fixtures add a 0.02 unit Box beside each sensor); pickable, objectType (ALL, NONE, one type), MATCH_ANY, MATCH_EVERY and MATCH_ONLY_ONE with one matching type, visible false; a sensor of objectType ALL sees through any group; a group of type ALL is seen by every sensor (as X_ITE 16.6.0); MATCH_EVERY and MATCH_ONLY_ONE with two matching types follow 19775-1 (every type of the sensor must be in the group, exactly one must be); X_ITE 16.6.0 counts at most one match, so those two steps run in ours only

PixelTexture3D.note: Babylon side: a WGSL ShaderMaterial over a RawTexture3D, shaded by the headlight (when NavigationInfo.headlight is TRUE) and by up to four lights that are on, as one-sided Lambert terms on the viewer-facing side; a spot light acts as a point light (no cone) and no light has attenuation, radius or global scope for a volume; compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 on a lit PixelTexture3D box with a DirectionalLight and a PointLight (silhouette 0.95, mean abs diff 3.0 of 255, Chromium 153 SwiftShader); TextureProperties anisotropy and mipmaps are not applied to volumes
PixelTexture3D.prev_note: Babylon side: a WGSL ShaderMaterial over a RawTexture3D, shaded by the headlight only (N dot view axis, two sided); other lights, TextureProperties anisotropy and mipmaps are not applied to volumes

PlaneSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 numerically (translation_changed, trackPoint_changed, offset, the routed box): plane drag, axisRotation 0 0 1 0.5, line mode (minPosition.x = maxPosition.x), clamp, disabled; agree within 0.1 relative on a 2 unit drag (the engines pick the press half a pixel apart); isOver is picked once per animation frame and keeps its value while a drag is active (the press owns the pointer); X_ITE does the same; line mode with both minPosition components equal turns the line along the sensor's y axis (X_ITE's first branch); translation_changed is in the sensor's own frame, as X_ITE reports it
PlaneSensor.prev_note: axisRotation is implemented (frame turned by it) but not exercised against X_ITE; trackPoint_changed is not compared: X_ITE reports it in the sensor frame, ours in the sensor frame at the press, to be checked; isOver (hover) is not raised by the drag sensors

PointLight.note: attenuation is a Babylon range cut at 1/32 of the polynomial (a0 1 0 0 means no fall-off), not X_ITE's per pixel polynomial; global=FALSE scope uses includedOnlyMeshes of the parent group; compared in our body only; ambientIntensity is not used; radius is a hard edge in X3D: Babylon has only a smooth range, so the range stays open and a mesh wholly beyond the radius is left out of the light (per mesh); a mesh that straddles the edge, like a big wall, is lit whole where X_ITE cuts a disc; checked by the colour of the spheres beyond it in both engines

PointPickSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in scene mode: sensors in a Transform with a Shape sibling (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not traverse a group that holds only a pick sensor, so the fixtures add a 0.02 unit Box beside each sensor); PointSet points inside a Box, a Sphere and a PickableGroup of another objectType; pickedPoint compared as a set (0.001), BOUNDS and GEOMETRY; pickedPoint holds the points of the PointSet in the sensor's frame, one entry per point inside a picked target (as X_ITE 16.6.0); with sortOrder CLOSEST or ANY only the reported target's points are listed

PointProperties.note: WebGPU has no point size: a PointSet with PointProperties is drawn as camera-facing squares whose size is clamp(pointSizeScaleFactor / (a + b d + c d^2), min, max) pixels (d = distance from the eye); X_ITE draws its points through its own point shader and much dimmer on this CPU raster, so size is not compared in the picture

Polyline2D.note: lines are not pickable, so the check is the picture (silhouette overlap and the mean colour of the drawn pixels, SwiftShader CPU raster) plus the segment count between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs through its internal getVertices, a private API) and one line mesh in our body; line width is one pixel in both, ours is an anti-aliased ribbon
Polyline2D.prev_note: lines are not pickable: the segment count is compared between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs via its private getVertices); colour and width are not compared

Polypoint2D.note: WebGPU has no point size: each point is a small camera-facing square drawn by a shader; X_ITE 16.6.0 draws its points much dimmer on this CPU raster (seen in the picture), colour and size are not compared; PointProperties sizing is not applied
Polypoint2D.prev_note: points cannot be picked: the point count is compared between the engines; WebGPU draws each point one pixel, X_ITE draws them with its point size; colour is not compared

PositionChaser.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

PositionChaser2D.note: end state only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

PositionDamper.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

PositionDamper2D.note: end state only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

PrimitivePickSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in scene mode: sensors in a Transform with a Shape sibling (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not traverse a group that holds only a pick sensor, so the fixtures add a 0.02 unit Box beside each sensor); BOUNDS and GEOMETRY (Sphere against Box where the boxes overlap and the geometries do not), sortOrder CLOSEST / ANY / ALL / ALL_SORTED, objectType filter, pickable false, enabled false; a shape outside every PickableGroup is not pickable here (as 19775-1 asks); X_ITE 16.6.0 picks it, the fixture checks it in ours only; disabling a sensor that is active raises isActive false here; X_ITE 16.6.0 keeps it true, checked in ours only; a Sphere picking geometry is a 162 point hull (0.4 percent inside the true sphere); the target is the convex hull of its mesh, so a concave target counts as its hull, as in X_ITE 16.6.0; the hull of the pickingGeometry is made when first needed and cached by geometry node, so a pickingGeometry node that is replaced is picked up on the next timestamp; non-uniform scale on the sensor is applied to the hull

ProgramShader.note: no shader language runs: the node is only a holder; ShaderProgram parts of programs are checked with the ShaderProgram node

ProjectionVolumeStyle.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 projects per slice, not along the whole ray, and the bridge copies it: the numbers (AVERAGE of a uniform volume is 38, MIN with no hit is white) are X_ITE, not the projection the specification describes; the march direction is the view direction in volume axes, not divided by the dimensions (as in X_ITE), so a volume with unequal dimensions projects along a different line than its shape suggests; only cubes are tested; a projection value near a layer boundary (the sample at 0.37537 against the edge at 0.375) depends on the exact slice plane; the fixture keeps the layers thick and probes one centre pixel per volume; a ProjectionVolumeStyle inside a Composed, Blended or the style list of an isosurface or segmented volume is dropped (it is not composable)

ProtoInstance.note: ExternProtoDeclare is not loaded (external files); an instance of one is dropped with a warning; an SFNode field connected through IS to two places is copied, so a DEF inside it exists twice; IS inside a nested ProtoInstance connects values only (as fieldValue), not events; getNodeTypeName on an instance returns the type of its first inner node, not the PROTO's name; a PROTO field that is an SFNode or MFNode is not reachable through the instance's SAI object (initializeOnly values are not exposed either way in X_ITE's SAI, so the tests do not read them)

QuadSet.note: attrib is read and kept; only a shader program would consume it, and no shader language runs in the bridge (see ShaderProgram, ProgramShader)

ReceiverPdu.note: bboxDisplay draws a wire cube in X_ITE (even with visible false) and does not in the bridge; bboxSize of a PDU does not reach the parent bounding box in X_ITE; a PDU accepts no children (the reader warns and drops them), as in X_ITE

Rectangle2D.note: the texture coordinates are the unit square; they are not compared with X_ITE

RigidBody.note: the bridge engine is its own (see RigidBodyCollection); the inertia field is ignored, the inertia is worked out from the shapes, as X_ITE's Bullet does; centerOfMass, finiteRotationAxis, useFiniteRotation, autoDamp, autoDisable and massDensityModel are kept but have no effect

RigidBodyCollection.note: the bridge engine is its own: sequential impulses at 240 Hz, spheres and boxes (cylinder and cone stand in as bounding spheres), one friction and bounce for the whole collection; autoDisable, disableTime and the disable speeds are kept but never put a body to sleep; centerOfMass is kept and not used; joints come in their own batch; contactSurfaceThickness, preferAccuracy and set_contacts are kept; CollisionSensor/Contact nodes come later

ScalarChaser.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

ScalarDamper.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

ScreenFontStyle.note: the node is not drawn: the Text font path of the body reads FontStyle only, and a screen font size in pixels (pointSize) is not applied; a ScreenFontStyle changes the text size with the content scale of the screen in X_ITE; none of this is reproduced

ScreenGroup.note: three pictures agree with X_ITE 16.6.0 on place and size (bounding boxes within 1 px; silhouette iou 0.93, mean difference 1.7 of 255 on Chromium 153.0.8010.12 SwiftShader / Babylon 9.32.0); X_ITE's picture has an anti-aliased ring of about one pixel that the body's does not, which is what the iou below 1 measures (bound iou 0.9); the pixel size comes from the depth of the group's origin only, as in X_ITE: the nearer face of a deep child looks a little larger; no snapping to whole pixels (X_ITE does not snap for ScreenGroup either); the device content scale is taken as 1 (X_ITE multiplies by its ContentScale)
ScreenGroup.prev_note: the pixel size comes from the depth of the group's origin only, as in X_ITE: the nearer face of a deep child looks a little larger; no snapping to whole pixels (X_ITE does not snap for ScreenGroup either); the device content scale is 1

Script.note: scripts are OFF unless the page sets R.bridge.allowScripts = true (they run code that comes with the scene); the test pages set it; shutdown(), node-valued fields, directOutput, external script files and the less common methods of the classic vector classes are not provided

SegmentedVolumeData.note: X_ITE reads the segment as int(r * 255), which truncates; the bridge rounds (no difference for exact ids, and none for a 1 voxel texture of ids with nearest filtering); the segment ids are read through the texture's own filtering, so a segmentIdentifiers volume of 16 or more voxels across is blended at the segment borders in both engines

ShadedVolumeStyle.note: the gradient is taken one voxel either side of the sample in the red channel, so a volume with no empty margin has no gradient at its border and draws nothing (as in X_ITE); only the headlight and up to three more lights act; their attenuation, radius and spot cone are not applied (X_ITE applies them); shadows and phaseFunction are kept and not used (X_ITE does not use them either); anisotropic dimensions tilt X_ITE's normals differently from the bridge's (the bridge divides the gradient by the dimensions); the test uses a cube

ShaderProgram.note: no shader language runs: the program is a holder; the 4.0 UOM lists a sourceCode field that X_ITE 16.6.0 does not have and the XSD cannot write; it is not offered

SignalPdu.note: the sample data is held and never played; no AudioContext is created; bboxDisplay: see ReceiverPdu

SilhouetteEnhancementVolumeStyle.note: a constant volume draws nothing with this style whatever the parameters (X_ITE 16.6.0 drops every sample with no gradient); the opacity is the alpha of a sample times the factor; nearly-saturating stacks hide small errors, so the faint case is the one that discriminates

SingleAxisHingeJoint.note: minAngle, maxAngle, stopBounce and stopErrorCorrection are applied by the bridge (one-sided limit rows); X_ITE 16.6.0 makes a btHingeConstraint without limits, so it ignores them (see the limit fixture lines); angle is signed in the bridge and unsigned in X_ITE (the angle of the axis-angle rotation); angleRate comes from the angle change over the time since the last tick; X_ITE multiplies by the frame rate

SliderJoint.note: separation is measured along the axis between the two body origins, as in X_ITE's slider; sliderForce is applied by the bridge as a force along the axis; X_ITE 16.6.0 reads the field and never applies it; stopBounce is kept and not used by the slider

SpatialSound.note: a SpatialSound plays only while it is drawn in X_ITE (its traversed flag, which a Switch or culling turns off); the bridge plays it whenever it is enabled; spatialize is an initializeOnly field: set at load, bypassing the panner; the routing is not read back; dopplerEnabled and priority are held; Web Audio has no doppler and there is one voice per node; a maxDistance of 0 or less is refused by Web Audio (RangeError): the old distance stays; X_ITE 16.6.0 raises the error inside its event handler, so the test does not try it; the HRTF response itself (inter-aural delay and spectrum) is compared only as the level of the two ears
SpatialSound.prev_note: a SpatialSound plays only while it is drawn in X_ITE (its traversed flag, which a Switch or culling turns off); the bridge plays it whenever it is enabled; spatialize is an initializeOnly field: set at load, bypassing the panner; the routing is not read back; dopplerEnabled and priority are held; Web Audio has no doppler and there is one voice per node; a maxDistance of 0 or less is refused by Web Audio (RangeError): the old distance stays; X_ITE 16.6.0 raises the error inside its event handler, so the test does not try it

SphereSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 numerically: trackPoint_changed agrees within 0.01 inside the sphere, within 0.02 where the pointer leaves the sphere (tangent plane rule) and for a press on the far half (sensor origin in front of the shape); rotation_changed: the angle agrees within 0.015 rad; after two drags the axis differs by up to 0.2 in one component: X_ITE's press hit lies about half a pixel off the pointer ray ((0.016, 0.016, 1) at the box centre, seen in its first trackPoint_changed) where ours is the pick at the pointer ((0, 0, 1)), and the composition offset * rotation amplifies it; the test bounds it at 0.25; isOver is picked once per animation frame and keeps its value while a drag is active
SphereSensor.prev_note: after the second drag the rotation angle agrees with X_ITE 16.6.0 (0.5205 vs 0.5235 rad) but one axis component differs by 0.2: the hit point of a press on an already turned box is read differently, not chased (no pixel perfection); trackPoint_changed not compared; a drag that leaves the sphere uses the nearest point of the sphere to the ray; X_ITE does the same by its own rule, only tested inside the sphere

SpotLight.note: the cone is a projection texture over tan(angle) (a Babylon SpotLight with its own exponent 0), full inside beamWidth and a linear ramp in the angle down to cutOffAngle as 19775-1 gives it; X_ITE and ours agree on the picture; two lights of the same angles share no texture (each light makes its own 256 x 256 table); attenuation and radius as on PointLight; a spot with cutOffAngle above about 88 degrees is held at 88 (a projection texture needs a cone under 180 degrees); Babylon only marks the projection of a SpotLight for update when the light's own position or direction changes, not when a parent Transform moves it: the bridge sets the (internal) dirty flag every frame; this is Likely stable on 9.32.0 but not a public API

StaticGroup.note: the static children are drawn as a Group and are not merged into one mesh as X_ITE does at load; the merge is an optimisation, it changes no field and no picture (compared below)

StreamAudioDestination.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 does nothing with this node (not supported), so the stream is checked against Web Audio only, in our reader; the stream is read back inside the same page (not sent over a network); mediaDeviceID has no meaning for a stream and is held; how a page uses the stream (a WebRTC connection, a recorder) is the page's business
StreamAudioDestination.prev_note: no network stream is made: streamIdentifier and mediaDeviceID are held

StreamAudioSource.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 does nothing with this node (not supported): no sound is made there and the sound is checked against Web Audio only, in our reader; the stream comes from inside the same page (a StreamAudioDestination or a stream the page adds), a stream from the network (WebRTC) is the page's to connect and is not tested; a stream that is added to the table after the node started is found within one frame
StreamAudioSource.prev_note: no stream is read: streamIdentifier is held

StringSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 step for step: typing, Backspace (also on an empty string and with deletionAllowed false), Enter, Escape, Tab, a typed string with a space, shifted letters; IME and dead-key composition are not handled by either engine: both read keydown only (X_ITE 16.6.0 KeyDeviceSensorComponent registers keydown and keyup), so a composed character arrives only if the browser also reports it as a key
StringSensor.prev_note: IME and dead-key composition are not handled (the browser reports one key at a time)
