SurfaceEmitter.note: colour is compared: a quad particle is lit like a surface (emissive + diffuse x headlight, white for this Material); ours is 255 white, X_ITE 16.6.0's mean over its drawn pixels is about 200 (its edges are blended), fg tolerance 70; no fade at the end of life without a colorRamp (as X_ITE); particle age at the shot differs between the engines on this CPU raster (ours runs on elapsed time at about 3 frames per second under SwiftShader), so the extent is compared with a wide bound; the emission point is a random point of the surface triangles, area weighted, along the face normal (a Sphere is cut into 16 x 12 facets for this)
SurfaceEmitter.prev_note: particle age at the shot differs between the engines on this CPU raster (ours runs on elapsed time at about 3 frames per second under SwiftShader), so the extent is compared with a wide bound; X_ITE 16.6.0 draws the particles white on this raster, ours uses the Material emissive colour (colour is not compared); the emission point is a random point of the surface triangles, area weighted, along the face normal (a Sphere is cut into 16 x 12 facets for this)

TexCoordChaser2D.note: end state only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

TextureBackground.note: ImageTexture and PixelTexture faces are drawn and compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 by pixel probes (right and bottom faces are PixelTextures); MovieTexture faces are not drawn (a video element is not read for a background); transparency lowers the alpha of the sky and the six faces (checked in ours only); what shows through is the body's clear colour, which the stock Background node still sets from its first Background, where X_ITE shows the page behind; the sky sphere has 48 segments and a ring every 1/32 of PI plus one at every angle, so a gradient is stepped finer than the eye sees; colours are linear between rings; the sky is a sphere of radius 900 around the camera, the six faces a cube of half-size 500 inside it; scenes with a camera far clip below 900 would cut it (the body uses at least 2000)
TextureBackground.prev_note: only ImageTexture faces are drawn (the stock texture reader); PixelTexture and MovieTexture faces are not; transparency lowers the alpha of the sky and the six faces (checked in ours only); what shows through is the body's clear colour, which the stock Background node still sets from its first Background, where X_ITE shows the page behind; the sky sphere has 48 segments and a ring every 1/32 of PI plus one at every angle, so a gradient is stepped finer than the eye sees; colours are linear between rings; the sky is a sphere of radius 900 around the camera, the six faces a cube of half-size 500 inside it; scenes with a camera far clip below 900 would cut it (the body uses at least 2000)

TextureCoordinateGenerator.note: the seven modes of the fixture are compared in the picture with X_ITE 16.6.0 (silhouette overlap 0.98, mean abs diff 13 of 255 over the whole frame on Chromium 153 SwiftShader) and against the formula in our body; the CAMERASPACENORMAL and CAMERASPACEREFLECTIONVECTOR spheres differ visibly from X_ITE (X_ITE's own scaling of the camera-space range is not reproduced); NOISE and NOISE-EYE are made from X_ITE's Perlin2.glsl (the same 2D value noise and cosine smoothing, parameter = scale xyz and translation xyz); the hash is fract(sin(..) * 43758.5453), which a GPU's float32 sin and JavaScript's double sin evaluate differently, so the picture shows the same kind of pattern, not the same pixels (the centre sphere of the fixture); camera-space modes are recomputed on the CPU whenever the model-view matrix changes, not in a shader
TextureCoordinateGenerator.prev_note: the six modes of the fixture are compared in the picture (silhouette overlap 0.98) and against the formula in our body; the CAMERASPACENORMAL and CAMERASPACEREFLECTIONVECTOR spheres differ visibly from X_ITE 16.6.0 (mean RGB difference 11 of 255 over the picture): X_ITE's own scaling of the camera-space range is not reproduced; camera-space modes are recomputed on the CPU whenever the model-view matrix changes, not in a shader; NOISE and NOISE-EYE are not made

TextureProjector.note: WebGPU only: the projection is WGSL code added by a Babylon MaterialPluginBase to the Standard and PBR materials of the world; a WebGL engine draws the scene without it; a shape drawn by a ShaderMaterial (a textured UnlitMaterial, points, lines, volumes) is not tinted; X_ITE 16.6.0 tints those too; the PBR path (PhysicalMaterial: surfaceAlbedo is tinted before the lights) compiles but was not compared by picture: PhysicalMaterial draws black in the body on this rig with or without a projector, so no tint can show; upVector default: X3DUOM 4.0 says 0 1 0 (used here); X_ITE 16.6.0 reads 0 0 1 for a scene whose version is 4.0 or lower, so a tilted projector with no upVector written is rolled differently there; at most four projectors at a time (X_ITE's maxTextures), the first four that are on; the picture is read nearest-texel, mip levels and TextureProperties filters are not applied (X_ITE's default look is nearest as well); a face of an unlit shape that turns away from the projector: X_ITE 16.6.0 still tints a thin visible side strip of an unlit slab, the bridge does not (compare 'back', fg tolerance 20)

TextureProjectorParallel.note: WebGPU only: the projection is WGSL code added by a Babylon MaterialPluginBase to the Standard and PBR materials of the world; a WebGL engine draws the scene without it; a shape drawn by a ShaderMaterial (a textured UnlitMaterial, points, lines, volumes) is not tinted; X_ITE 16.6.0 tints those too; the PBR path (PhysicalMaterial: surfaceAlbedo is tinted before the lights) compiles but was not compared by picture: PhysicalMaterial draws black in the body on this rig with or without a projector, so no tint can show; upVector default: X3DUOM 4.0 says 0 1 0 (used here); X_ITE 16.6.0 reads 0 0 1 for a scene whose version is 4.0 or lower, so a tilted projector with no upVector written is rolled differently there; at most four projectors at a time (X_ITE's maxTextures), the first four that are on; the picture is read nearest-texel, mip levels and TextureProperties filters are not applied (X_ITE's default look is nearest as well); shadows, shadowColor, shadowIntensity and shadowMapSize are stored and do nothing (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not shadow a projector either)

TextureTransform3D.note: the moved strip (left) is compared by its matrix in our body only: X_ITE 16.6.0 draws it as a mostly flat colour, while its own TextureTransformMatrix3D with the same matrix (fixture TextureTransformMatrix3D) agrees with ours, so X_ITE's TextureTransform3D field handling differs from the 4.0 text (tc' = T C R S -C tc), Likely; the picture comparison covers the unmoved strip; the whole picture against X_ITE 16.6.0: silhouette 0.99, mean abs diff 1.6 of 255 (Chromium 153 SwiftShader), the moved strip is a flat colour in X_ITE and a gradient in ours
TextureTransform3D.prev_note: the moved strip (left) is compared by its matrix in our body only: X_ITE 16.6.0 draws it as a mostly flat colour, while its own TextureTransformMatrix3D with the same matrix (fixture TextureTransformMatrix3D) agrees with ours, so X_ITE's TextureTransform3D field handling differs from the 4.0 text (tc' = T C R S -C tc), Likely; the picture comparison covers the unmoved strip

ToneMappedVolumeStyle.note: the colours' alpha is not used (the voxel alpha stays); with no light the colour is black; only the headlight and up to three more lights act, with no attenuation or cone

TransformSensor.note: the official x3d-4.0.xsd cannot express TransformSensor.targetObject (containerField is limited to children, proxy, rootNode, shape, skin), so the fixture leaves it out and the test sets it through the SAI; compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 numerically (position_changed and orientation_changed within 0.001): target at the root, sensor under a translated and rotated Transform that is then moved again, target a Shape (its group's matrix), size 0 0 0 (never active) and -1 -1 -1 (always active); the sensor runs once per timestamp, so a moved target is seen one frame late
TransformSensor.prev_note: the sensor frame is its parent's; a parent that itself moves is followed through the world matrix, tested only with the root; a target that is a Shape uses its group's matrix; the official x3d-4.0.xsd cannot express TransformSensor.targetObject (containerField is limited to children, proxy, rootNode, shape, skin), so the fixture leaves it out and the test sets it through the SAI

TransmitterPdu.note: bboxDisplay: see ReceiverPdu; radio transmission is not simulated

TriangleFanSet.note: attrib is read and kept; only a shader program would consume it, and no shader language runs in the bridge (see ShaderProgram, ProgramShader)

TriangleSet2D.note: compared by pointer-over probes, the triangle count and the picture; X_ITE 16.6.0 culls the clockwise second triangle although solid is false, ours draws it facing +z (the 4.0 text: a 2D geometry has no back side), a deliberate difference
TriangleSet2D.prev_note: compared by pointer-over probes in both engines and the triangle count; the clockwise second triangle is turned to face +z in ours, X_ITE draws it two-sided

TwoSidedMaterial.note: with a light that adds ambient (ambientIntensity 0.6) and TwoSidedMaterial.ambientIntensity 1 on the sphere, our picture is brighter at the sphere's edge than X_ITE 16.6.0's (mean abs diff 4.9 of 255 against 2.5 with the default 0.2, Chromium 153 SwiftShader); ours follows 19775-1 (ambient = light ambientIntensity x material ambientIntensity x diffuseColor), X_ITE appears not to take the value (Suspected, not isolated); backAmbientIntensity is read and not compared; which side shows which colour is compared in the picture with X_ITE 16.6.0 (the lower row is turned round, so it shows the back colours; a solid=TRUE pair in the middle is culled in both engines; silhouette 0.98, mean abs diff 2.5 of 255 on SwiftShader), and in our body by pass: two meshes for solid=FALSE, one for solid=TRUE; the specular highlight of the sphere follows Phong shininess*128 and is compared in the picture
TwoSidedMaterial.prev_note: which side shows which colour is compared in the picture (the lower row is turned round, so it shows the back colours; a solid=TRUE pair in the middle is culled in both engines), and in our body by pass: two meshes for solid=FALSE, one for solid=TRUE; ambient and ambientIntensity are read and not shown (no ambient term in the headlight model); the specular highlight of the sphere follows Phong shininess*128 and is compared in the picture

UniversalJoint.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 does not support UniversalJoint or MotorJoint; the bridge solves them (anchors meet, axes at 90 degrees); stop1Bounce, stop1ErrorCorrection, stop2Bounce and stop2ErrorCorrection are kept and not used

ViewpointGroup.note: the proximity box is tested in the frame of the group's parent (a Transform above moves it); the test moves a group with a Transform and compares the list with X_ITE 16.6.0; retainUserOffsets is held; X_ITE 16.6.0 reads it only on the viewpoint nodes, never on a ViewpointGroup; the page decides how to show the list; the stock pages have none, so Body.viewpointList() is the only way to read it (X_ITE: getUserViewpoints)
ViewpointGroup.prev_note: the proximity box is tested in world coordinates: a ViewpointGroup under a moved Transform is tested as if the Transform were not there; retainUserOffsets is held but not applied (the stock body keeps no user offsets per viewpoint); the page decides how to show the list; the stock pages have none, so Body.viewpointList() is the only way to read it

Viewport.note: the layer's viewport (clip rectangle) and a Viewport node in the world are compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 as pictures (silhouette iou 1.0, mean difference 1.3 to 1.6 of 255 on Chromium 153.0.8010.12 SwiftShader / Babylon 9.32.0; bound iou 0.97, mad 4): in a layer the rectangle is the layer's own projection, in the world the projection of the whole canvas is squeezed into the rectangle (both as X_ITE does); a Viewport in the world is drawn by a camera of its own over the world, with the depth cleared between the two; X_ITE keeps one depth buffer, so a world object in front of the Viewport's content is not hidden behind it here (not compared); a pointer outside the rectangle does not reach the layer or the Viewport's children (compared with TouchSensors); XSD finding: x3d-4.0.xsd (x3d_mcp) takes a Viewport as the viewport of a layer, not as a child of Scene or a group; the world-level fixture is checked against the XSD plus one line (xsdAllow, the receipt names it)
Viewport.prev_note: a Viewport used as a grouping node of the world builds its children but does not clip them (Babylon has one viewport per camera; the world's camera is shared); the layer's picture is squeezed into the clip rectangle, not cut out of the full picture: the same as X_ITE's viewport, which also changes the aspect

VisibilitySensor.note: occlusion by other shapes is not tested, by either engine (X_ITE 16.6.0 tests the frustum only); compared with X_ITE: inside, behind the camera, beyond the side plane, a box straddling the side plane (active), just outside (inactive), centre moved out and back, enabled false and true; one decision per frame; enterTime and exitTime are the frame timestamps
VisibilitySensor.prev_note: occlusion by other shapes is not tested (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not test it either); one decision per frame; enterTime and exitTime are the frame timestamps

VolumeData.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 draws 400 view-aligned slices with no opacity correction; the bridge marches a ray on the same planes but accumulates in float where X_ITE blends 8 bit per slice, so a volume of faint alpha differs by tens of levels (the tests check saturated colours); bboxSize and bboxCenter are kept and change nothing (they only matter for culling, as in X_ITE); opaque shapes that cut through a volume are not cut per pixel (the box is depth tested as a whole); fog and clip planes are not applied to the volume

VolumePickSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in scene mode: sensors in a Transform with a Shape sibling (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not traverse a group that holds only a pick sensor, so the fixtures add a 0.02 unit Box beside each sensor); Cylinder and IndexedFaceSet tetrahedron as picking geometry, BOUNDS and GEOMETRY against a Box and a Sphere; picking geometries the body cannot read as vertices (anything beyond the primitives, IndexedFaceSet, IndexedTriangleSet, PointSet, line sets) never pick; the sensor stays inactive; GEOMETRY is a convex hull test (GJK); a concave picking geometry counts as its hull

WaveShaper.note: oversample is compared against X_ITE only (the aliasing energy above 8 kHz agrees within 0.01), not against an ideal band limited reference; the curve is held to Float32 as in Web Audio
WaveShaper.prev_note: the curve is read back by length and by values, the shaping itself is Web Audio's
